import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Filter for significant features (p < 0.05)
    sig_idx = [i for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids) if 
               abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[:, i][feats.y==0], feats.x[:, i][feats.y==1]).statistic) > 2.0]
    
    if not sig_idx:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Compute correlation matrix
    X_sig = feats.x[:, sig_idx]
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(X_sig.T)
    
    # Handle case where we have very few significant features
    if corr_matrix.shape[0] < 2:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Cluster features with high correlation
    clustering = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=min(2, corr_matrix.shape[0]), linkage='average')
    clusters = clustering.fit_predict(1 - np.abs(corr_matrix))  # Convert to distance
    
    # Find the cluster with more features (likely the module)
    cluster_sizes = np.bincount(clusters)
    main_cluster = np.argmax(cluster_sizes)
    
    # Get features in the main cluster
    module_features = [feats.ids[i] for i in sig_idx if clusters[i - sig_idx[0]] == main_cluster]
    
    if len(module_features) < 2:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Create weighted score using first two features
    w1, w2 = 0.5, 0.5
    weights = {module_features[0]: w1, module_features[1]: w2}
    
    # Add interaction term
    products = [(module_features[0], module_features[1])]
    
    return Design(
        drivers=(module_features[0],),
        columns=tuple(module_features),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=weights
    )
